rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap
rawCommits.body:
After SessionReady, `useNewSessionUrlSync` did two things in sequence:

  1. `optimisticRow.swap(<real-id>)` — synchronously rewrote the
     `optimistic:<uuid>` row in `sessionsBySurface` to the
     server-assigned UUID via Zustand `setState`.
  2. `setSearchParams({ session: <real-id> })` — queued a React
     Router navigate.

`SessionsList`'s `effectiveSelectedSessionId` only had two cases — URL
session, or fall back to the optimistic row. The window between those
two writes (and any subsequent render where the router state hadn't
propagated through `useSearchParams` yet — back/forward, suspended tab,
etc.) had neither: the row was no longer `optimistic:` and `?session=`
hadn't landed, so the just-created session visibly appeared at the top
of the list with its server-generated title but read as unselected.
The user reported this as "after sending message in new session, still
does not select it in the css".

Add a third fallback: when the URL has no `?session=` and no optimistic
row exists, highlight `titledRows[0]` — the newest row in the surface.
The surfaces are stored in `sortSessionsDesc` order from
`loadAgentSessions` / `loadProjectSessions`, and `addOptimisticSession`
stamps `started_at` at insert time, so the just-swapped real-id row
always sorts to the top across the swap window. Pre-swap, the
optimistic branch still wins; once the URL settles, the explicit
`selectedSessionId` branch wins again.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap

rawCommits.subject: feat(swarm): auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error
rawCommits.body:
When a brand-new remote agent's background readiness wait timed out or
saw `state: error`, the only effect was a `warn!` in the desktop log:
the agent stayed in `provisioning`, the UI sat indefinitely on
"Starting up...", and the user had to manually click Recovery (often
not even knowing the agent was stuck). The cause string supplied by
aura-swarm (e.g. an `Unschedulable` PodScheduled message) was also
dropped because `SwarmAgentStateResponse` only deserialized `state`,
so any error event the gateway emitted was reduced to a generic
"entered error state".

Changes:

- Widen `SwarmAgentStateResponse` to include `error_message` and
  carry the optional reason through `SwarmAgentReadyError::ErrorState`
  and `PollOutcome::Errored`.
- Replace the inert `warn!()` branches in `spawn_swarm_readiness_check`
  with `auto_recover_after_initial_failure`, which broadcasts an
  `auto_recover/starting` event, runs the existing
  `recover_remote_agent_pipeline` exactly once, and on failure
  broadcasts a terminal `state: "error", phase: "startup_failed"`
  carrying both the original swarm reason and the recovery error so
  the StatusCard exits the indeterminate provisioning state and shows
  the manual Recovery action.
- Update `handle_recovery_readiness_error` to embed the swarm-supplied
  reason in both the broadcast banner and the `ApiError`, so the
  manual Recovery click also surfaces the descriptive cause.
- Pass enough context (cloned `AppState`, `Arc<NetworkClient>`,
  `NetworkAgent`) through `BackgroundReadinessTask` to invoke recovery
  from the spawned task.
- Add `starting` and `startup_failed` entries to the StatusCard
  `PHASE_NOTICES` so the UI labels match the new broadcast phases.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error

rawCommits.subject: feat(agent-picker): add searchable AgentSelectorList with keyboard nav
rawCommits.body:
New `AgentSelectorList` component renders the Telegram-style picker
the next step will mount inside `AgentSelectorModal`. The list shows a
'Standard Agent' row at the top followed by every saved fleet agent,
filtered live by the search query (case-insensitive over name + role).

Keyboard model mirrors `SlashCommandMenu`:
- Up/Down move the active highlight, wrapping at the edges
- Enter activates the highlighted row
- Escape calls the supplied `onCancel`
- Mouse hover updates the active index
- Rows fire on `mouseDown` with `preventDefault` so the search input
  keeps focus when a row is clicked

The component is purely presentational; it forwards a ref so the
parent modal can hand it the focus target via `Modal.initialFocusRef`.
Per-row `creating` state shows a spinner on the row mid-create and
disables every row to prevent double-fires.

rawCommits.subject: chore(changelog-media): tag credit-low errors with the failing provider
rawCommits.body:
The publish-release-changelog-media workflow calls three different paid
APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Browser Use). When one runs out of credits, the
previous wording made it ambiguous which account actually needed a top-up
- e.g. "You need at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34" with
no provider name attached.

Route every HTTP/SDK failure in the pipeline through a shared helper that
prefixes the failing provider and names the env var to top up:

  [Browser Use] credit balance is too low (top up the account tied to
  BROWSER_USE_API_KEY - https://cloud.browser-use.com/billing): You need
  at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34

Non-credit failures also pick up the provider tag so CI logs always
identify the source.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: tag credit-low errors with the failing provider

rawCommits.subject: chore(changelog-media): downgrade Browser Use credit-low to a warning
rawCommits.body:
Previously a low Browser Use balance crashed the entire
publish-release-changelog-media workflow at the first capture
attempt - even though the rest of the pipeline (planner, report,
manifest) had nothing to do with that account. The pipeline is
already best-effort (the desktop release and text changelog ship
before this workflow even runs), so the right behavior is to skip
the Browser Use flow for the cycle and exit cleanly.

runChangelogMediaEvaluation now wraps the runBrowserUseTaskImpl call:
when wrapProviderError raises a `[Browser Use]` credit-low error
(providerCreditError === true && provider === "browser-use"), the
current candidate becomes a `blocked` result with the credit message
in `blockers[]`, a `browser-use-credit-exhausted` progress event
fires, and a flag short-circuits every remaining candidate so the
SDK isn't called again. Non-credit Browser Use failures still throw.

The report and stdout summary now carry `browserUseCreditExhausted`,
`browserUseCreditMessage`, and `counts.captureSkippedForCredits`, and
the script exits 0 - so the downstream "Publish accepted media into
gh-pages" step finds an empty manifest and no-ops cleanly instead of
the whole job going red.

Regression test plans two candidates, has runBrowserUseTaskImpl
throw a credit-tagged error, and asserts the SDK is called exactly
once while both candidates land as blocked with the credit blocker.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: downgrade Browser Use credit-low to a warning

rendered.title: Searchable agent picker, sturdier provisioning, and a calmer media pipeline
rendered.intro: Today's nightly reshapes how you add agents to a project — the old card grid is gone, replaced by a Telegram-style searchable list with keyboard navigation and a one-keystroke Standard Agent shortcut. Around that headline change, remote agent startup now self-heals once before bothering you, the Windows installer's theme handling got two real fixes, and the release-media workflow stops taking the whole job down when a third-party API runs out of credits.

entries.title: Add Agent picker rebuilt as a searchable list
entries.summary: The project Add Agent flow is now a single Telegram-style picker with search, keyboard nav, and a one-press Standard Agent shortcut — plus fixes to session selection and the Windows installer's themed assets.

items.text: Replaced the grid-of-cards AgentSelectorModal with a new searchable AgentSelectorList: autofocused search, a Standard Agent row pinned to the top, arrow-key + Enter navigation, hover sync, and per-row spinners during create. The old '+ Create New Agent' footer and separate AgentEditorModal are gone — pressing Enter on the Standard row hits the same default-create endpoint the project '+' used to fire silently.

Fixed a sessions bug where a brand-new chat would briefly read as unselected after the optimistic→real id swap; SessionsList now falls back to the newest row in the surface during that window so the just-created session stays highlighted.

Remote agents that fail their initial provisioning readiness check now auto-recover once in the background and, if that still fails, surface the real swarm reason (e.g. Unschedulable PodScheduled) in both the StatusCard banner and manual Recovery errors instead of hanging on 'Starting up…'.

Windows installer now stages dark and light themed bitmaps directly into $PLUGINSDIR (no more root-relative writes from .onInit), swaps the header bitmap at GUI init in light mode, applies the dark title-bar hook to the uninstaller, and fails the build with a clear error if the bitmap naming convention is broken. Chat attachments also now accept .json and .sql files.

entries.title: Picker polish, project navigation, and a CEO-only capability fix
entries.summary: Follow-up fixes harden the new Add Agent modal, improve project sidebar navigation, add a GLB download to the 3D viewer, and roll back an accidental 'all agents get full access' regression.

items.text: Reverted a regression where every newly created agent inherited full_access capabilities; the blanket empty→full_access promotion is now restricted to the CEO bootstrap, and non-CEO agents once again start with an empty bundle and opt in via the Permissions tab.

Add Agent modal no longer gets stuck: stale busy state could trap users by blocking Close/Escape and disabling Create indefinitely — close always works now and Create is only disabled during an active API call.

Project sidebar auto-expands to reveal the active agent when you navigate into a project (e.g. switching from the Agents app), and session rows now show the project name when sessions span multiple projects.
Chat now shows a helpful error when an agent has no project assigned instead of failing silently, and the aura3d WebGL viewer gained a Download button to save the generated GLB.

entries.title: Windows uninstaller GUI-init callback fix
entries.summary: Unblocked makensis builds that were aborting on the uninstaller's GUI-init hook.

items.text: Renamed the uninstaller's GUI-init callback to use the required `un.` prefix (AuraUnOnGUIInit → un.AuraOnGUIInit) so MUI_LANGUAGE no longer aborts expansion of MUI_UNFUNCTION_GUIINIT, with an inline note documenting the NSIS constraint to prevent regressions.

entries.title: Project agent picker stabilization and Terminal-by-default sidekick
entries.summary: A second pass on the new picker stops it from resizing or flashing empty mid-selection and shows the full org fleet; Projects also reliably lands on the Terminal tab again.

items.text: Agent picker now passes the active org id to api.agents.list() so teammates' shared agents appear (matching the Agents app sidebar), locks the modal's vertical footprint with a 360px floor across loading/empty/list states, and keeps the just-selected row visible through the create+handoff transition to prevent the 'No agents match your search.' flash.

Projects' sidekick panel now forces the Terminal tab on app entry, so a previous click on Sessions — or writes from the Tasks app or spec-generation stream — no longer sticks across reloads. Switching tabs inside a session still persists as before.
Renamed the project sidebar's agent context-menu action to 'Remove from Project' to match the existing modal copy and make the project-scoped nature of the action obvious.

entries.title: Changelog-media pipeline tolerates Browser Use credit outages
entries.summary: Release-media CI no longer goes red when a paid API runs out of credits — failures are clearly tagged by provider and Browser Use credit exhaustion now degrades gracefully.

items.text: Every Anthropic, OpenAI, and Browser Use call in the publish-release-changelog-media pipeline now routes through a shared helper that prefixes the failing provider and names the env var to top up (e.g. `[Browser Use] credit balance is too low (top up the account tied to BROWSER_USE_API_KEY …)`), so CI logs always identify which account needs attention.

A low Browser Use balance used to crash the entire workflow on the first capture; it now flips remaining candidates to a `blocked` result with the credit message, emits a `browser-use-credit-exhausted` progress event, exits 0, and lets the downstream gh-pages publish step no-op cleanly. Non-credit failures still throw.

highlights: Remote agents auto-recover once on provisioning failure
Windows installer themed-bitmap and uninstaller fixes
Changelog media pipeline survives Browser Use credit outages
